catering_flightline.label: Catering & flight-line items
catering_flightline.note: metal items such as cans or pens count as hard

rules.text: The engine intake zones (ENG-L, ENG-R) must be free of FOD.
The pushback path and nose-gear area (NOSE) must be free of FOD.
The service zones (CARGO, AFT) must be cleared of FOD before departure.
rules.basis: FAA AC 150/5210-24A §3.3.1, §4.3.1.1.3 (advisory); 14 CFR §139.305(a)(4) (binding on the airport)

rules.text: FOD on the stand perimeter (WIDE only): hard or unidentified items must be removed; light or natural items are logged.
An object that can't be identified is treated as FOD at its zone's severity.
Every required Angle must be usable. Otherwise the Verdict is INCOMPLETE.
Snow, ice, spills and live wildlife are non-FOD hazard observations, kept out of the FOD Verdict.
GSE, chocks, cones and tow bars in their normal positions are not FOD. Loose or misplaced ones are.
At pre-arrival, GSE must be staged behind the equipment restraint line.
rules.basis: IATA IGOM 4.1.1(d) (industry standard); ATL staging violation classes (airport rule)

rules.text: FOD outside the gate safety envelope is reported, not removed by the ramp crew: shared taxilane to Ramp 1 control (for AATC), movement area to Airport Operations.
